finding.claim: purge() never enforces the admin permission: checkPerm's boolean result is discarded, so any caller whose request context carries a User (any permission level) can trigger the destructive purgeAll() operation.
finding.source: Any request reaching the purge handler with a *User in its context (handlers.go:25 userFrom(r)). The user's Perms map is attacker-influenced only through their own account, so any authenticated low-privilege user satisfies the precondition.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 (destructive, protected operation; stub here, real implementation lives outside this directory).

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) obtains the user from request context; no nil/permission check follows.
checkPerm(u, "admin") is called but its bool return is discarded; it is a no-op guard.
checkPerm itself is correct (returns u.Perms[perm]), so the defect is the missing use of its result at the call site.
purgeAll() executes unconditionally for any caller that reached this line.
Writes "purged" with 200 status on success, confirming the protected action completed for the non-admin caller.

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14): returns a value, but the value is ignored at line 26, so it is not a control. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22): not invoked by purge(); the correct pattern exists in rotateKeys (line 33) but was not applied. Upstream authentication middleware and route registration are NOT in this directory, so whether unauthenticated callers can reach purge is unverified; the finding assumes at least authenticated low-privilege access. No CSRF, method, or rate-limit controls are visible for this handler. Fix: `if !mustPerm(w, u, "admin") { return }` before purgeAll().

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-13) returns u.Perms[perm], but its result is discarded at handlers.go:26 as a bare statement, so it is not enforced. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) exists and would return false and write 403, but purge() never calls it (rotateKeys at handlers.go:33 does). No other guard in this directory; upstream route/middleware is not visible.
verdict.reason: purge() calls checkPerm(u, "admin") at handlers.go:26 as a bare statement, discarding the bool, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any request whose context holds a *User (userFrom at handlers.go:25 panics on a missing user, so the precondition is an authenticated user of any role); the admin check the handler intends is not enforced. The one residual uncertainty is whether route registration outside this directory restricts purge to admins, which I cannot see.
